sentences.text: ORAL ORDER 1.

The present application is filed under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, for regular bail in connection with the FIR being C.R. No.I-611/2001 registered with the 'B' Division Police Station, Rajkot for the offence punishable under Sections 363, 366, 376 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.
2. Learned advocate for the applicant submits that the incident has occurred on 18.09.2001, for which, FIR has been lodged on 22.09.2001 and the present applicant has been arrested on 12.09.2023.

It is submitted that FIR is registered against in all three accused persons including the present applicant and except present applicant, against other two co-accused, the investigation was completed and the chargesheet was filed and, NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18073/2023 ORDER DATED: 19/10/2023

undefined thereafter, the trial was proceeded against them and at the end of trial, said two-accused have been acquitted by the concerned Sessions Court considering the material and evidence available on record against them.
It is submitted that the role attributed to the present applicant is that he has abetted the co-accused in the alleged commission of crime.

It is,

1 therefore, urged that considering the above factual aspects of the matter, the present application may be allowed by imposing suitable conditions.
3. Learned APP for the respondent-State has opposed grant of regular bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.

Learned APP submitted that the role of the present applicant is spelt-out from the evidence as he has supported the main accused persons and the present applicant has saved his skin from the clutches of the IO to avoid his arrest.
It is, therefore, urged that the present application may not be entertained.
4. Learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties do not press for further reasoned order.

5. I have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of the respective parties and perused the papers of the investigation and considered the allegations levelled against the applicant and the role played by the applicant.

It is found out from the record that the offence is of the year 2001 and the present applicant is arrested recently on NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/18073/2023 ORDER DATED: 19/10/2023 undefined 12.09.2023.
It is further found out that other two co-accused have been acquitted by the concerned Sessions Court on conclusion of the trial and the role attributed to the present applicant is of abettor.
Thus considering overall facts of the case, the present application deserves to be allowed.

6. This Court has also taken into consideration the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sanjay Chandra v. Central Bureau of Investigation, reported in [2012] 1 SCC 40 as well as in case of Satender Kumar Antil v. Central Bureau of Investigation & Anr. reported in (2022) 10 SCC 51.
7.
